# ggstack

> Interactive CLI (`create-ggstack`) that scaffolds a pnpm + Turborepo monorepo in the T3/Turbo style. Pick Vite, Next.js, Astro, Expo Router, Electron, Express, Fastify, TanStack Start, and/or React Router, then optionally add shadcn/ui, tRPC, Better Auth / Clerk / WorkOS, Stripe / Polar / Autumn, Resend + React Email, and Drizzle or Prisma (PostgreSQL, MySQL, or SQLite). Every project gets a typed `packages/env` and a root `.env.example`.

This file is the full user guide concatenated for language models. Prefer it over HTML docs pages. Source of each section: `apps/docs/guide/`. The docs site also serves each page as Markdown at the same path with a `.md` suffix, plus `/llms.txt` (index) and `/llms-full.txt` (this bundle).

`create-ggstack` is the published npm package. This repository also contains the VitePress docs (`apps/docs`) and the CLI source (`apps/create-ggstack`). It is **not** a generated app — it *writes* generated apps.

Create a project from a visual builder (`--stack` skips prompts):

```bash
pnpm create ggstack@latest my-app --stack g1e30
cd my-app
cp .env.example .env
pnpm install
pnpm dev
```

Build `--stack` codes at `/create`. Inspect one with `pnpm create ggstack --decode <code>`. Also accepted: `npx create-ggstack my-app --pnpm` or `pnpm dlx create-ggstack my-app`. Interactive mode: `pnpm create ggstack my-app`.

---

# Getting Started

`create-ggstack` is an interactive CLI. It writes a pnpm workspace with Turborepo, a typed env package, and the apps and packages you select.

## Requirements

- Node.js 22 or newer
- [pnpm](https://pnpm.io) — the generated monorepo uses pnpm workspaces even if you pass `--npm`, `--yarn`, or `--bun`

## Create a project

The fastest path is the visual builder: pick your stack, copy the command, paste it in a terminal.

1. Open `/create`
2. Choose apps, packages, auth, database, payments, email, and tooling
3. Copy the generated command. It looks like this:

```bash
pnpm create ggstack@latest my-app --stack g1e30
```

`--stack` packs the whole config into a short code and skips every prompt. Share the builder URL to send someone the same setup. Inspect a code with `pnpm create ggstack --decode <code>`.

You can still run the CLI interactively:

```bash
pnpm create ggstack
```

Or pass a directory name:

```bash
pnpm create ggstack my-app
```

Other runners:

```bash
npx create-ggstack my-app --pnpm
pnpm dlx create-ggstack my-app
```

Without `--stack`, the CLI prompts for apps, package extras (including a shadcn base and, if you want one, a preset when shadcn/ui is on), tooling, auth, a database ORM, a payment provider (Stripe, Polar, or Autumn), an email provider (Resend), and — when you pick Drizzle or Prisma — which database to use. You can also pass a shadcn preset on the command line with `--preset <code>`. See CLI.

## After the CLI finishes

```bash
cd my-app
cp .env.example .env
pnpm install
pnpm dev
```

`pnpm dev` runs Turbo `dev` across apps that define that script (Vite, Next.js, Astro, Electron, Express, Fastify, TanStack Start, React Router). Expo uses `start` instead — run it from the app package. Fill in `.env` before anything that reads `packages/env`; validation fails on empty required values unless you skip it. Details are in Environment.

The scaffolded repo also gets a `README.md` that lists what you selected and the same next steps.

---

# CLI

```text
create-ggstack [project-name] [options]
```

## Options

| Flag | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `--stack <code>` | Full stack from the `/create` page. Skips every prompt. |
| `--decode [code]` | Print the decoded `--stack` config and exit. Accepts `--decode <code>` or `--stack <code> --decode`. |
| `--preset <code>` | shadcn/ui preset: a named style (`nova`, `luma`, …) or a code from [ui.shadcn.com/create](https://ui.shadcn.com/create). Enables shadcn/ui. Combined with `--stack`, this overrides the stack’s shadcn preset. |
| `--pnpm` | Use pnpm to run official app CLIs (default) |
| `--npm` | Use npm to run official app CLIs |
| `--yarn` | Use yarn to run official app CLIs |
| `--bun` | Use bun to run official app CLIs |
| `-h`, `--help` | Print help |
| `-v`, `--version` | Print the package version |

```bash
pnpm create ggstack@latest my-app --stack g1e30
pnpm create ggstack my-app --preset b2D0vQ7G4
pnpm create ggstack --decode g1e30
```

Also accepted: `--stack=g1e30` and `--preset=b2D0vQ7G4`. Build `--stack` codes visually on `/create`. The code packs apps (including Vite framework/variant and folder names), packages, shadcn base/preset, tooling, auth, database, payments, email, and the package manager used to run official app CLIs. Project name stays a positional argument. `--preset` without `--stack` still skips only the preset-code prompt and keeps shadcn/ui on even if you deselect it in the packages list. `--npm`, `--yarn`, and `--bun` override the package manager stored in a `--stack` code.

`--npm`, `--yarn`, and `--bun` only affect package-manager invocations the CLI runs during scaffold. The generated repo is still a **pnpm workspace**. The CLI warns when the flag is not `--pnpm`. You still need pnpm installed to work in the project.

## Interactive flow

1. **Project name** — positional argument, or a prompt (default `project`). The default is shown as grey placeholder text and is used if you press Enter without typing.
2. **Apps** — multi-select, optional: Vite, Next.js, Astro, Expo Router, Electron + Vite, Express, Fastify, TanStack Start, React Router.
3. **App names** — one prompt per selected app. Defaults: `vite`, `next`, `astro`, `expo`, `electron`, `express`, `fastify`, `tanstack-start`, `react-router`. Same grey placeholder as the project name.
4. **Vite framework** — if you selected Vite: Vanilla, Vue, React, Preact, Lit, Svelte, Solid, or Qwik. TypeScript only; JavaScript variants are not offered.
5. **Vite variant** — if the Vite framework is React: TypeScript, or TypeScript + React Compiler. Other frameworks skip this prompt.
6. **Packages** — multi-select, optional: shadcn/ui, tRPC.
7. **shadcn component base** — if you selected shadcn/ui (or passed `--preset`): Base UI (default), Radix UI, or React Aria.
8. **shadcn preset** — if you selected shadcn/ui and did not pass `--preset`: "Do you want to use a shadcn preset?" Default no. No prints that the CLI is using the default config (`nova`) and continues. Yes asks for a named style (`nova`, `vega`, `maia`, `lyra`, `mira`, `luma`, `sera`, `rhea`) or a code from [ui.shadcn.com/create](https://ui.shadcn.com/create). Skipped when `--preset` is already on the command line.
9. **Tooling** — multi-select: Tailwind CSS, Oxc, Prettier, ESLint. Tailwind is pre-selected (and always kept) if shadcn/ui is on. Selecting Tailwind installs Tailwind CSS v4 once in `tooling/tailwind` and wires it into frontend apps. Expo also gets NativeWind.
10. **Authentication** — Better Auth, Clerk, WorkOS, or none (default none).
11. **Database ORM** — none (default), Drizzle, or Prisma. Choosing an ORM adds `packages/db`.
12. **Database** — if you chose Drizzle or Prisma: PostgreSQL (default), MySQL, or SQLite. Drizzle hints name the driver (`node-postgres`, `mysql2`, `libsql`). Prisma hints name the `schema.prisma` `provider`.
13. **Payments** — none (default), Stripe, Polar, or Autumn. Choosing a provider adds `packages/payments`.
14. **Email** — none (default) or Resend. Choosing Resend adds `packages/email` with React Email templates and a Resend sender.

`packages/env`, `tooling/tsconfig`, and a root `.env.example` are always written.

## Names

Project and app names go through the same sanitizer: lowercase, spaces become hyphens, characters outside `a-z`, `0-9`, and `-` are stripped, leading and trailing hyphens are removed. App names in one project must be unique after sanitizing.

## Abort conditions

The CLI exits without writing files when:

- The chosen package manager is not installed
- `--stack` is passed with no value, or with a value that is not a `g1…` stack code
- `--preset` is passed with no value, or with a value that is not a named style or preset code
- The target directory already exists

---

# Project

A generated repo is a pnpm workspace with Turborepo. Workspace globs are `apps/*`, `packages/*`, and `tooling/*`.

## Layout

```text
my-app/
├── .env.example          # always; copy to .env
├── .gitignore
├── .npmrc                # engine-strict=true
├── package.json
├── pnpm-workspace.yaml
├── turbo.json
├── README.md
├── apps/
│   ├── vite/             # optional Vite (framework chosen in the CLI)
│   ├── next/             # optional Next.js
│   ├── astro/             # optional Astro
│   ├── expo/             # optional Expo Router
│   ├── electron/         # optional Electron + Vite
│   ├── express/          # optional Express
│   ├── fastify/          # optional Fastify
│   ├── tanstack-start/   # optional TanStack Start
│   └── react-router/     # optional React Router
├── packages/
│   ├── env/              # always
│   ├── ui/               # optional shadcn/ui
│   ├── api/              # optional tRPC
│   ├── auth/             # optional, when an auth provider is selected
│   ├── db/               # optional, when Drizzle or Prisma is selected
│   ├── payments/         # optional, when Stripe, Polar, or Autumn is selected
│   └── email/            # optional, when Resend is selected
└── tooling/
    ├── tsconfig/         # always
    ├── tailwind/         # optional
    ├── oxc/              # optional
    ├── prettier/         # optional stub
    └── eslint/           # optional stub
```

App folder names are whatever you typed (after sanitizing), not the type names above.

## `.gitignore`

The root `.gitignore` is generated from the apps, tooling, and database dialect you selected. Workspace entries are always present: `node_modules`, `dist`, `.turbo`, `**/.cache/`, `*.log`, `.env`, and `.env.local`.

Stack-specific paths are added only when that choice is on:

| Selection | Entries |
| --- | --- |
| Next.js | `.next`, `out` |
| Astro | `.astro` |
| Expo Router | `.expo`, `expo-env.d.ts`, `web-build` |
| Electron + Vite | `release` |
| TanStack Start | `.output`, `.nitro`, `.tanstack` |
| React Router | `.react-router`, `build` |
| ESLint | `.eslintcache` |
| Prettier | `.prettiercache` |
| Drizzle + SQLite | `*.db`, `*.db-journal`, `*.db-wal`, `*.db-shm` |

Vite, Express, Fastify, shadcn/ui, tRPC, auth, payments, email, PostgreSQL/MySQL Drizzle, Prisma, Tailwind, and Oxc do not add extra ignore paths — they use `dist`, `.env`, or `node_modules` already listed in the workspace section. Drizzle + SQLite also ignores `*.db`, `*.db-journal`, `*.db-wal`, and `*.db-shm`. Astro build output is `dist`; only the generated `.astro` types directory is extra.

## Root scripts

| Script | What it runs |
| --- | --- |
| `pnpm dev` | `turbo run dev` |
| `pnpm build` | `turbo run build` |
| `pnpm lint` | `turbo run lint`, or repo-wide Oxc if you selected Oxc |
| `pnpm format` | `turbo run format`, or repo-wide Oxc format if you selected Oxc |
| `pnpm check-types` | `turbo run check-types` |
| `pnpm test` | `turbo run test` |

Turbo `dev` is uncached and persistent. `check-types` depends on `^build`. Env vars from `packages/env` are listed on `turbo.json` `globalEnv` (except `NODE_ENV`).

## Package manager

Install and run scripts with **pnpm**. The generated `package.json` pins `packageManager` to `pnpm@11.2.2` when you scaffolded with pnpm. Node is declared as `>=22` (`engine-strict` is on).

Filter a single package:

```bash
pnpm --filter @apps/next dev
pnpm --filter @packages/db db:studio
```

Workspace package names follow the folder they live in: `@apps/<folder>`, `@packages/<folder>`, and `@tooling/<folder>`. The project name is not used as a scope.

---

# Apps

Apps are optional. You can scaffold packages and tooling with no apps.

Each selected app is copied from a static template shipped with the CLI. Every app depends on `@packages/env`.

## Vite

TypeScript Vite app (`vite` ^8). After you select Vite, the CLI asks for a framework. JavaScript variants are not offered.

| Framework | Variant prompt | Plugin / extra |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Vanilla | none (TypeScript) | none |
| Vue | none (TypeScript) | `@vitejs/plugin-vue`, `vue-tsc` |
| React | TypeScript, or TypeScript + React Compiler | `@vitejs/plugin-react` |
| Preact | none (TypeScript) | `@preact/preset-vite` |
| Lit | none (TypeScript) | `lit` |
| Svelte | none (TypeScript) | `@sveltejs/vite-plugin-svelte`, `svelte-check` |
| Solid | none (TypeScript) | `vite-plugin-solid` |
| Qwik | none (TypeScript) | `@builder.io/qwik` (`qwikVite({ csr: true })`) |

React Compiler is an overlay on the React template: it adds `@rolldown/plugin-babel`, `babel-plugin-react-compiler`, `@babel/core`, and `@types/babel__core`, and wires `reactCompilerPreset()` in `vite.config.ts`.

Scripts: `dev`, `build`, `preview`. Vue uses `vue-tsc --noEmit` for `check-types`; Svelte uses `svelte-check`.

`vite.config.ts` calls `createViteEnv(import.meta.env)` so client vars with the `VITE_` prefix are validated at config load.

```bash
pnpm --filter @apps/vite dev
```

Default port: `5173`. Default folder name is still `vite`; the framework only changes the files inside that app.

## Astro

Astro 7 + TypeScript. Scripts: `dev` (`astro dev`), `build` (`astro build`), `preview`, `check-types` (`astro check`).

`astro.config.ts` imports `@packages/env/server` so server env is validated when Astro starts. Client vars use the `PUBLIC_` prefix (`astroEnv`).

```bash
pnpm --filter @apps/astro dev
```

Default port: `4321`.

## Next.js

Next.js 16 + React 19 App Router. Scripts: `dev`, `build`, `start`.

`next.config.ts` imports `@packages/env/server` so server env is validated when Next starts.

```bash
pnpm --filter @apps/next dev
```

## Expo Router

Expo SDK 57 + Expo Router. Scripts: `start`, `ios`, `android`, `web`. There is **no** `dev` script, so this app does not join root `pnpm dev`.

`app/_layout.tsx` imports `expoEnv` from `@packages/env/client`.

When Tailwind is selected, NativeWind v5 is added to the Expo app. Styling comes from the shared `@tooling/tailwind` package (`tailwindcss` is not installed in the Expo app). `app/_layout.tsx` imports `../global.css`, Metro is wrapped with `withNativewind`, and the home screen uses `className`.

```bash
pnpm --filter @apps/expo start
```

## Electron + Vite

Electron + Vite + vanilla TypeScript. Scripts: `dev` (Vite), `build` (`tsc && vite build && electron-builder`), `preview`.

The main process reads optional `VITE_DEV_SERVER_URL` from `serverEnv`. Vite injects that URL during desktop `dev`.

```bash
pnpm --filter @apps/electron dev
```

## Express

Express 5 + TypeScript. Scripts: `dev` (`tsx watch`), `start` (`tsx`), `build` (`tsc --noEmit`).

`src/index.ts` imports `@packages/env/server` so server env is validated when the process starts. Default port: `3001` (`process.env.PORT` overrides it). Routes: `GET /`, `GET /health`.

```bash
pnpm --filter @apps/express dev
```

## Fastify

Fastify 5 + TypeScript. Scripts: `dev` (`tsx watch`), `start` (`tsx`), `build` (`tsc --noEmit`).

`src/index.ts` imports `@packages/env/server` so server env is validated when the process starts. Default port: `3002` (`process.env.PORT` overrides it). Routes: `GET /`, `GET /health`.

```bash
pnpm --filter @apps/fastify dev
```

## TanStack Start

TanStack Start + Vite + React 19. Scripts: `dev` (`vite dev`), `build` (`vite build`), `preview`.

`vite.config.ts` imports `@packages/env/server` and calls `createViteEnv(import.meta.env)` so both server and `VITE_` client vars are validated at config load.

```bash
pnpm --filter @apps/tanstack-start dev
```

Default port: `3003`.

## React Router

React Router 8 framework mode + Vite + React 19. Scripts: `dev` (`react-router dev`), `build` (`react-router build`), `start` (`react-router-serve`).

`vite.config.ts` imports `@packages/env/server` and calls `createViteEnv(import.meta.env)` so both server and `VITE_` client vars are validated at config load.

```bash
pnpm --filter @apps/react-router dev
```

Default port: `5174`.

## Auth and database

App templates do **not** wrap `AuthProvider` or import `@packages/db`. After you add those packages, import them in the app yourself. See Packages.

---

# Packages

## `packages/env` (always)

Typed env via `@t3-oss/env-core` and Zod. Exports:

| Import | Use |
| --- | --- |
| `@packages/env/server` | `serverEnv` — Node/server variables |
| `@packages/env/client` | `nextEnv`, `astroEnv`, `expoEnv`, and/or `createViteEnv`, plus `getPublicAuthConfig()` for Clerk/WorkOS |
| `@packages/env` | Re-exports server and client |

Add new variables in the Zod schemas **and** in the root `.env.example`. Full matrix: Environment.

```ts
import { serverEnv } from "@packages/env/server";

const url = serverEnv.DATABASE_URL;
```

## `packages/ui` (shadcn/ui)

Created when you select shadcn/ui, or when you pass `--preset`. Tailwind is forced on. After you pick the package, the CLI asks for a **component base**, then whether you want a **preset** (unless `--preset` was already passed).

| Prompt / flag | Default | What it sets |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Component base | Base UI | Primitive library: Base UI, Radix UI, or React Aria. Written as the `style` prefix (`base-nova`, `radix-nova`, `aria-nova`). |
| Do you want to use a shadcn preset? | No | No keeps the default config (`nova`) and says so. Yes asks you to paste a named style (`nova`, `vega`, `maia`, `lyra`, `mira`, `luma`, `sera`, `rhea`) or a short code from [shadcn/create](https://ui.shadcn.com/create). You can also pass `--preset <code>`. The code packs colors, theme, fonts, radius, and icon library. |

What you get:

- Latest shadcn CLI (`shadcn@^4.18.0`) plus `class-variance-authority`, `clsx`, `tailwind-merge`, and `lucide-react`
- `components.json` using the current schema: `{base}-{style}` (not the deprecated `default` style), CSS variables, `baseColor: neutral`, `iconLibrary: lucide`, aliases for `components` / `ui` / `utils` / `lib` / `hooks`, Tailwind v4 with empty `config`
- Theme CSS path points at `tooling/tailwind/src/theme.css` so tokens stay shared
- `src/lib/utils.ts` with `cn()`
- `src/globals.css` importing `@tooling/tailwind`
- `src/index.ts` re-exports `cn()` — no components are pre-generated

If you paste a custom preset code (not a named style), scaffold runs `shadcn@latest apply --preset <code> --yes` in `packages/ui` so the official CLI writes the theme.

Add components from the repo root:

```bash
pnpm --filter @packages/ui add button
```

Or:

```bash
pnpm dlx shadcn@latest add button -c packages/ui
```

Then export them from `src/index.ts`. Switch themes later with `pnpm --filter @packages/ui apply --preset <code>`. Partial apply (`--only theme` or `--only theme,font`) keeps your components and only updates tokens or fonts.

## `packages/api` (tRPC)

Created when you select tRPC. Exports:

| Import | Use |
| --- | --- |
| `@packages/api` | `appRouter`, `AppRouter`, `createTRPCContext`, `createCaller` |
| `@packages/api/client` | `createApiClient(url)` — vanilla HTTP client |

Starter procedure: `hello.greet({ name?: string })` → `{ greeting }`.

If you also picked Drizzle or Prisma, context includes `db` / `prisma`. Add procedures after you define your own schema.

```ts
import { createCaller, createTRPCContext } from "@packages/api";

const caller = createCaller(await createTRPCContext());
const { greeting } = await caller.hello.greet({ name: "Ada" });
```

```ts
import { createApiClient } from "@packages/api/client";

const api = createApiClient("http://localhost:3000/api/trpc");
const { greeting } = await api.hello.greet.query({ name: "Ada" });
```

React Query is not included. Type-only import `AppRouter` and create the React client in the app:

```ts
import type { AppRouter } from "@packages/api";
import { createTRPCReact } from "@trpc/react-query";

export const api = createTRPCReact<AppRouter>();
```

**Not auto-wired.** Mount the router on a host after scaffold. Next.js App Router uses `@trpc/server/adapters/fetch` at `app/api/trpc/[trpc]/route.ts`. Express uses `createExpressMiddleware`. Fastify uses `fastifyTRPCPlugin`. See the generated `packages/api/README.md` for the snippets.

## `packages/auth` (optional)

Created when the auth provider is not `none`. Unified surface:

```tsx
import { AuthProvider, AuthDemo, useAuth } from "@packages/auth";

export default function App() {
  return (
    <AuthProvider>
      <AuthDemo />
    </AuthProvider>
  );
}
```

`useAuth()` returns `{ user, isAuthenticated, isLoading, signIn, signOut }`. Each provider also re-exports its SDK helpers.

| Provider | SDK | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Better Auth | `better-auth` | Client wrapper only. Add a Next.js route such as `app/api/auth/[...all]/route.ts` yourself. `signIn` on `useAuth` is a stub — call `authClient.signIn.social()` or send users to your sign-in page. |
| Clerk | `@clerk/clerk-react` | `AuthProvider` wraps `ClerkProvider` with the publishable key from `getPublicAuthConfig()`. |
| WorkOS | `@workos-inc/authkit-react` | `AuthProvider` wraps AuthKit with the client id from `getPublicAuthConfig()`. |

**Not auto-wired.** Wrap your app root with `AuthProvider` after scaffold.

## `packages/email` (optional)

Created when the email provider is not `none`. Shared React Email templates and a Resend sender live in `@packages/email`. **Not auto-wired** — call the helpers from a server route or job after scaffold. See the generated `packages/email/README.md` for snippets.

| Provider | SDK | What you get |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Resend | `resend` + `react-email` | Starter `WelcomeEmail` template, `sendEmail` / `sendWelcomeEmail` helpers, and `email:dev` preview on port 3001. |

```ts
import { sendWelcomeEmail } from "@packages/email";

await sendWelcomeEmail({
  to: user.email,
  name: user.name,
});
```

Preview templates:

```bash
pnpm --filter @packages/email email:dev
```

Pass templates as a function call (`WelcomeEmail({ name })`), not as JSX. Add new files under `src/emails` with a default export to see them in the preview sidebar.

## `packages/db` (optional)

Created when you pick Drizzle or Prisma.

### Drizzle

Exports `db`. The CLI asks which database to use and scaffolds the matching driver and `drizzle.config.ts` dialect. No starter tables — add them in `src/schema.ts`.

| Database | Driver |
| --- | --- |
| PostgreSQL (default) | `pg` + `drizzle-orm/node-postgres` |
| MySQL | `mysql2` + `drizzle-orm/mysql2` |
| SQLite | `@libsql/client` + `drizzle-orm/libsql` |

```ts
import { db } from "@packages/db";
```

### Prisma

Exports `prisma`. The CLI asks which database to use and sets `datasource.provider` in `schema.prisma` (`postgresql`, `mysql`, or `sqlite`). No starter models — add them in `prisma/schema.prisma`.

```ts
import { prisma } from "@packages/db";
```

Scripts (run from the repo root with a filter, or inside `packages/db`):

| Script | Drizzle | Prisma |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `db:generate` | `drizzle-kit generate` | `prisma generate` |
| `db:migrate` | `drizzle-kit migrate` | `prisma migrate dev` |
| `db:push` | `drizzle-kit push` | `prisma db push` |
| `db:studio` | Drizzle Studio | Prisma Studio |

```bash
pnpm --filter @packages/db db:push
```

Set `DATABASE_URL` first. **Not auto-wired** into app templates — import `@packages/db` where you need a query.

---

# Environment

Every project gets `packages/env` and a root `.env.example`. Copy that file to `.env` at the repo root and fill in values. `.env` is gitignored.

```bash
cp .env.example .env
```

The Zod schema is generated from the apps, auth provider, payment provider, email provider, and ORM you selected. Empty required strings fail validation.

## Server vs client

- **Server** vars live on `serverEnv` (`@packages/env/server`) and are read from `process.env`.
- **Client** vars use the prefix of each selected app family and are validated separately.

| App type | Client prefix | Client export |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Next.js | `NEXT_PUBLIC_` | `nextEnv` |
| Astro | `PUBLIC_` | `astroEnv` |
| Expo | `EXPO_PUBLIC_` | `expoEnv` |
| Vite, Electron, TanStack Start, or React Router | `VITE_` | `createViteEnv(runtimeEnv)` — pass `import.meta.env` |
| Express or Fastify | — | no client export; they import `@packages/env/server` on boot |

Clerk and WorkOS also generate `getPublicAuthConfig()`, which reads the publishable key / client id from whichever of those prefixed names is set.

## Variable matrix

| When | Name | Kind | Required |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Always | `NODE_ENV` | server | no (`development` \| `test` \| `production`) |
| Any database ORM (PostgreSQL or MySQL) | `DATABASE_URL` | server | yes (URL) |
| Any database ORM + SQLite | `DATABASE_URL` | server | yes (string, e.g. `file:./packages/db/local.db`) |
| Better Auth | `BETTER_AUTH_SECRET` | server | yes |
| Better Auth | `BETTER_AUTH_URL` | server | yes (URL) |
| Clerk | `CLERK_SECRET_KEY` | server | yes |
| Clerk + Next | `NEXT_PUBLIC_CLERK_PUBLISHABLE_KEY` | client | yes |
| Clerk + Astro | `PUBLIC_CLERK_PUBLISHABLE_KEY` | client | yes |
| Clerk + Vite/Electron/TanStack Start/React Router | `VITE_CLERK_PUBLISHABLE_KEY` | client | yes |
| Clerk + Expo | `EXPO_PUBLIC_CLERK_PUBLISHABLE_KEY` | client | yes |
| WorkOS | `WORKOS_API_KEY` | server | yes |
| WorkOS | `WORKOS_COOKIE_PASSWORD` | server | yes |
| WorkOS + Next | `NEXT_PUBLIC_WORKOS_CLIENT_ID` | client | yes |
| WorkOS + Astro | `PUBLIC_WORKOS_CLIENT_ID` | client | yes |
| WorkOS + Vite/Electron/TanStack Start/React Router | `VITE_WORKOS_CLIENT_ID` | client | yes |
| WorkOS + Expo | `EXPO_PUBLIC_WORKOS_CLIENT_ID` | client | yes |
| Electron | `VITE_DEV_SERVER_URL` | server | no (URL; injected in Electron dev) |
| Resend | `RESEND_API_KEY` | server | yes |
| Resend | `EMAIL_FROM` | server | yes (`Name <address@yourdomain.com>`) |

Better Auth extra secrets (for example `GITHUB_CLIENT_ID`) are not generated. Add them to the schema and `.env.example` if you need them.

## Skipping validation

Validation is skipped when any of these is true:

- `CI` is set
- `SKIP_ENV_VALIDATION=true`
- `npm_lifecycle_event` is `lint`

Those names, plus `NODE_ENV`, `VERCEL`, `VERCEL_ENV`, and `VERCEL_URL`, are listed on Turbo `globalPassThroughEnv`. Generated app/auth/db keys (except `NODE_ENV`) are listed on `globalEnv`.

---

# Tooling

`tooling/tsconfig` is always generated. Everything else is opt-in at the tooling prompt.

## TypeScript

`@tooling/tsconfig` ships `base.json`: `ES2022`, `moduleResolution: bundler`, `strict`, `noUncheckedIndexedAccess`, `verbatimModuleSyntax`. Apps and packages extend it.

## Tailwind CSS

Creates `tooling/tailwind` with Tailwind CSS v4 (`^4.3.3`) and a shared PostCSS plugin. `tailwindcss` is declared only in that package. Forced on when shadcn/ui is selected (the prompt pre-selects it and the generator keeps it even if you deselect it).

Frontend apps (Vite, Next.js, Astro, Electron, TanStack Start, React Router) get a `postcss.config.mjs` that re-exports `@tooling/tailwind/postcss` and an `@import "@tooling/tailwind"` in their CSS entry. They depend on `@tooling/tailwind`, not `tailwindcss`. Express and Fastify are left alone.

Expo is wired with NativeWind v5 on top of the same package: `withNativewind` in `metro.config.js`, `global.css` imported from `app/_layout.tsx`, and `lightningcss` pinned to `1.30.1` at the workspace root.

With shadcn, the shared `theme.css` includes the current CSS-variable color tokens (oklch, light and dark, charts, sidebar). `styles.css` also imports `tw-animate-css` and `shadcn/tailwind.css` from the latest `shadcn` package. A custom preset code is applied onto this file by `shadcn apply`.

## Oxc

Creates `tooling/oxc/oxlint.json` and `oxfmt.json`, and rewrites the **root** `lint` and `format` scripts to run Oxc across the repo:

```bash
pnpm lint    # oxlint --config tooling/oxc/oxlint.json .
pnpm format  # oxfmt --config tooling/oxc/oxfmt.json .
```

Default lint rule of note: `typescript/no-explicit-any` is an error. Format defaults: 2-space indent, semicolons, double quotes, trailing commas.

Selecting Oxc also adds `oxlint` and `oxfmt` to the root `devDependencies`.

## Prettier (stub)

Writes `tooling/prettier/.prettierrc.json` and installs Prettier at the repo root. It does **not** wire a root `format` script or editor integration. The CLI says “manual wiring still required.”

## ESLint (stub)

Writes `tooling/eslint/eslint.config.js` (flat config with ignore patterns only) and installs ESLint at the repo root. Same story: no root `lint` rewrite. Prefer Oxc if you want lint/format to work immediately.

---

# This repository

This GitHub repo is the CLI + docs, not a generated project.

| Path | What |
| --- | --- |
| `apps/create-ggstack` | Published CLI (`create-ggstack`) |
| `apps/docs` | VitePress site (Vercel) |
| `packages/ui` | Placeholder workspace package for this repo |
| `tooling/` | Shared Oxc + TypeScript config |
